name: Lateral meniscus — posterior horn
description: Posterior third of the lateral meniscus, from the popliteal hiatus to the root, about the size of the anterior horn; the meniscofemoral ligaments leave its back for the medial femoral condyle. At the hiatus the popliteus tendon separates it from the capsule, tethered by the popliteomeniscal fascicles.

normal_values.mfl_interface_extent_lateral_to_pcl: Humphry about 1, Wrisberg about 3 consecutive 3 mm sagittal images lateral to the PCL

variants_pitfalls: Meniscofemoral pseudotear: an oblique intermediate line where Humphry or Wrisberg joins the horn near the PCL, in 39–63% of knees. Extending 4 or more images lateral to the PCL, especially with an ACL tear, raises the possibility of a real tear; look for surfacing signal or distortion.
With an ACL tear, lateral tears are more often posterior and peripheral and easier to miss (sensitivity 69% vs 94%); check along the Wrisberg attachment.

Magic angle makes the upsloping medial segment intermediate on short-TE images in most knees, but T2 fading does not exclude a tear: surfacing signal on 2 or more short-TE slices, or distortion, is a tear.
Popliteus sheath fluid at the hiatus mimics a vertical peripheral tear; trace the tendon. Indistinct popliteomeniscal fascicles alone are not a tear (26–40% of controls).
